title: HWiNFO64 Telemetry: Thermal Throttle & Fan Max
symptom: HWiNFO64 Telemetry Log Analysis [sensor_log.txt]: System: Intel Core i7-11800H @ 2.30GHz, 16GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Laptop GPU, CPU Package Temperature: 99.4°C (Max: 100.0°C), CPU Core Thermal Throttling: Yes, CPU Power Limit / PROCHOT Reason: Yes, CPU Fan Speed: 4920 RPM, GPU Temperature: 68.2°C (Hotspot: 79.1°C), Battery Wear Level: 12.5%, Storage Drive Temp: 56.0°C. System exhibits severe thermal throttling under load.

expected_output.symptom_summary: HWiNFO64 telemetry indicates critical CPU core thermal throttling at 99.4°C and maximum fan RPM (4920 RPM) triggering hardware PROCHOT limits.

evidence.text: CPU Power Limit / PROCHOT Reason: Yes

possible_causes.cause: Compromised thermal interface material (TIM) pump-out or degradation causing extreme thermal junction delta.
possible_causes.verification: Inspect heatsink mounting tension and thermal paste viscosity across the CPU die.

possible_causes.cause: Cooling fin stack airflow obstruction preventing heat dissipation despite maximum fan RPM.
possible_causes.verification: Check exhaust port airflow velocity using a hand or anemometer to verify restriction.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Elevate rear chassis on a solid surface and inspect external cooling intake/exhaust vents.
Clean heatsink fins with compressed air while device is powered down.
troubleshooting_steps.rationale: Clears potential debris blankets causing the thermal block.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Consult technician to repaste the CPU/GPU with high-viscosity thermal compound.
troubleshooting_steps.rationale: Directly resolves high thermal resistance under PROCHOT conditions.
